questions.q: Match each kind of malware to what makes it that kind.
pairs: Attaches itself to a file and spreads when that file is opened
Copies itself across a network without anybody opening anything
Pretends to be a useful program so the user installs it
Encrypts the user's files and demands payment
Records what the user does and sends it to the attacker
questions.feedback: The difference between a virus and a worm is whether a person has to do anything.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a virus and a worm.

markPoints.concept: a virus attaches to a file and needs the user to open or run it
accept: attach|attaches|attached|part of a file|hides in|inside a file|user opens|user runs|somebody opens|someone opens|has to be opened|needs the user|relies on
markPoints.exemplar: A virus attaches to a file and spreads when the user opens it.

markPoints.concept: a worm copies itself across a network on its own
accept: copies itself|replicates|spreads itself|on its own|automatically|by itself|no user|without anybody|without the user|does not need the user|independently
markPoints.exemplar: A worm copies itself across a network without the user doing anything.

questions.example: A virus attaches itself to a file and only spreads when somebody opens or runs that file, whereas a worm copies itself across a network on its own without anybody having to do anything.
questions.paraphrase: A virus hides inside a file and relies on a person running it to spread, while a worm replicates itself over the network with no human involvement at all.
questions.feedback: Both halves. The distinction that earns marks is whether a user has to act.

questions.q: A user downloads what looks like a free photo editor. Once installed, it opens a back door for an attacker. What kind of malware is this?
questions.feedback: Pretending to be something useful is what makes it a Trojan.

questions.q: Which of these help protect a computer against malware? Tick all that apply.
options: Anti-malware software kept up to date
Not opening attachments from unknown senders
correct: Anti-malware software kept up to date
Not opening attachments from unknown senders
questions.feedback: Updates matter because most malware exploits a hole that has already been fixed.
